- When sentiment is strongly positive and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in such cases.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative (especially after a spike), model often overshoots downward; apply a lagged correction: subtract 1–3% of the previous day’s forecast.
- In periods of low news volume, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast tends to be too high; adjust downward by 1–3% relative to recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment change is negative and recent prices are falling, model often fails to recognize the trend; apply a “safety margin” to avoid underestimating the drop.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 10–15% below the 7-day moving average of the history.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to err on the high side — use sentiment change as a proxy: if sentiment change > 0.5, reduce forecast by 1–2%; if < -0.5, increase by 1–2% to compensate for lag.
